messages.content: Explain why ice floats on liquid water. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: Ice floats on liquid water because it is less dense than its liquid form. When water freezes, its molecules organize into a rigid, open crystalline structure held together by hydrogen bonds. This structure pushes the molecules further apart than they are in the liquid state, causing the water to expand as it turns to ice. Because this makes a given volume of ice lighter than the same volume of liquid water, the ice rises to the surface.
